extracted.intended_audience: hospital finance officers, Medicare contractors, hospital administrators, health policy stakeholders, and public commenters on the IPPS proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the standards and calculation rules CMS proposes for FY2027 inpatient prospective payment system (IPPS) and related capital payment rates, including outlier policy, standardized amounts, wage/COLA adjustments, and update framework components.

rubrics_metrics.name: No retroactive adjustment to outlier payments
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS does not make retroactive adjustments to outlier payments to ensure total outlier payments equal a target percentage (e.g., 5.1%) of MS-DRG payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: preserves prospective nature and predictability of IPPS; retroactive across-the-board adjustments would prevent hospitals from reliably approximating payment while patient is hospitalized. CMS cites statutory interpretation of section 1886(d)(5)(A)(iv) that references projected/estimated (not actual) MS-DRG payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlier payment projection target and statutory bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: The outlier threshold is set so that operating outlier payments are projected to be 5.1 percent of total operating IPPS DRG payments; statute indicates outlier payments be equal to or greater than 5 percent and less than or equal to 6 percent of projected or estimated MS-DRG payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use projected/estimated payments (not actual) when setting the outlier threshold; CMS will not retroactively force actual outlier payments to match the projection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of available MedPAR claims data with lag acknowledgement
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates of actual outlier payments rely on available MedPAR claims data; complete FY data (e.g., FY2026) will not be available until after Sept 30 of the FY year and thus cannot be estimated in the current proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS will provide later-year actual estimates in future rules (e.g., FY2026 actual outlier payments will be provided in FY2028 proposed rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized amount split and labor-related share proposed rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The adjusted standardized amount is divided into labor-related and nonlabor-related portions. CMS is proposing a national labor-related share of 62 percent for FY2027, with tables (1A/1B/1C) reflecting two possible labor-related shares (66% and 62%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory sections 1886(d)(3)(E) and 1886(d)(9)(C)(iv) guide application: apply 62% unless application would result in lower payments to a hospital; effectively apply 62% for hospitals with wage index ≤ 1.0000 and 66% for hospitals with wage index > 1.0000 per CMS proposal and accompanying tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor-related share application for Puerto Rico hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed labor-related and nonlabor-related portions for Puerto Rico are shown separately; statutory provision (as amended by Public Law 108‑173 sec.403(b)) provides that labor-related share for Puerto Rico be 62% unless application would lower payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply 62% labor-related share for Puerto Rico hospitals unless that percentage would result in lower payments to that hospital.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment for area wage levels (wage index application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 1886(d)(3)(E) and 1886(d)(9)(C)(iv) require adjustment to the labor-related portion by multiplying it by the appropriate wage index for the hospital's area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY2027 CMS proposes to apply a labor-related share of 66.0% for hospitals with wage index >1.0000 and 62% for those with wage index ≤1.0000; see preamble discussion and wage index methodology in section IV.B.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for Alaska and Hawaii (nonlabor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust the nonlabor-related portion of the standardized amount for hospitals in Alaska and Hawaii by a COLA factor to account for higher nonlabor costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically used OPM COLAs updated with CPI; for FY2027 CMS proposes to switch to Department of Defense Overseas Cost-of-Living Allowance (OCOLA) data effective Jan 1, 2026, believing OCOLA better captures nonlabor price differences including shipping to remote areas and reflects locality-specific prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology for selecting and averaging DOD OCOLAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use DOD OCOLAs for 26 Alaska and 6 Hawaii localities; map these to OPM-designated Nonforeign COLA Areas and average OCOLAs within a 50-mile radius of designated cities to produce COLA factors (e.g., Anchorage average of Anchorage and Wasilla OCOLAs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific averaging described: Anchorage (average Anchorage & Wasilla), Fairbanks (average College, Eielson AFB, Fairbanks), Rest of Alaska (average Bethel & Kenai), Maui/Kalawao (average Maui & Molokai). CMS will use four OPM Nonforeign COLA Areas for Alaska and four for Hawaii as before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of 25% COLA cap starting FY2027
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes to no longer cap COLA factors at 25 percent (the statutory OPM cap previously incorporated by CMS) beginning in FY2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because CMS is moving away from OPM COLAs to DOD OCOLAs, it is exercising discretionary authority to remove the 1.25 cap. CMS will continue updating COLAs on the same cadence as the labor-related share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation of comments on DOD OCOLA use and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS solicits comments on use of DOD OCOLAs, including concerns about Service member survey specificity, potential differential impacts, and on possible methodology modifications and phase-in/transitional approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public comments may influence finalization in the FY2027 IPPS/LTCH PPS final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prospective payment rate calculation steps
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS provides a 6‑step process to calculate operating and capital prospective payment rates and outlier payments for each claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps are used both for actual claim payment and to project outlier thresholds, with some variables sourced differently for projections (e.g., adjusted CCRs and MedPAR charges with inflation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 — MS‑DRG and relative weight determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the MS‑DRG and MS‑DRG relative weight for each claim primarily based on the ICD‑10‑CM diagnosis and ICD‑10‑PCS procedure codes on the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Table 5 (MS‑DRG relative weights) as referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 — Select applicable average standardized amount
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the applicable average standardized amount depending on whether the hospital submitted qualifying quality data and is a meaningful EHR user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different standardized amounts apply based on quality and EHR participation as described earlier in the rule; see tables in Addendum section VI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 3 — Compute Federal payment rates (operating and capital)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute operating and capital Federal payment rates using formulas that incorporate MS‑DRG relative weight, labor- and nonlabor-related standardized amounts, wage index/COLA, IME, DSH, geographic adjustment, and Federal capital rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating formula: MS‑DRG RW × [(Labor-Related Standardized Amount × CBSA Wage Index) + (Nonlabor Standardized Amount × COLA)] × (1 + IME + (DSH * 0.25)). Capital formula: MS‑DRG RW × Federal Capital Rate × Geographic Adjustment Fact × (1 + IME + DSH).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 4 — Derive operating and capital costs via CCRs
rubrics_metrics.description: Operating Costs = Billed Charges × Operating CCR; Capital Costs = Billed Charges × Capital CCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For actual claim payment CCRs come from PSF; for projections CMS uses adjusted CCRs described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 5 — Compute outlier thresholds (operating and capital)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute operating and capital outlier thresholds using CCR share ratios, fixed-loss threshold, geographic adjustments, and add-ons (IME, DSH, uncompensated care, supplemental payments, new technology add-on).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating CCR to Total CCR = Operating CCR / (Operating CCR + Capital CCR). Operating Outlier Threshold = [Fixed Loss Threshold × ((Labor Portion × CBSA Wage Index) + Nonlabor Portion)] × Operating CCR to Total CCR + Federal Payment with IME, DSH + Uncompensated Care Payment + supplemental payments + New Technology Add‑On. Capital Outlier Threshold analogous using Capital CCR share and geographic adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 6 — Compute outlier payments using marginal cost factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlier payments equal (Costs − Outlier Threshold) × Marginal Cost Factor, where Marginal Cost Factor = 0.80 or 0.90 depending on the MS‑DRG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute separately for operating and capital: Operating Outlier Payment = (Operating Costs − Operating Outlier Threshold) × Marginal Cost Factor; Capital Outlier Payment similar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of other payments in outlier calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: When calculating outlier thresholds and payments, CMS includes uncompensated care payments, supplemental payments for eligible IHS/Tribal hospitals and Puerto Rico hospitals, and new technology add-on payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are added to the Federal Payment amount considered in the outlier threshold formula (i.e., they affect whether a case exceeds the fixed-loss threshold).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of different CCR sources for claims vs projections
rubrics_metrics.description: Actual claim payment CCRs are from the PSF while CMS uses an adjusted CCR to project the outlier threshold for the upcoming fiscal year; charges for claim payment are from the bill while charges to project the threshold are from MedPAR with an inflation factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the source differences when reproducing projection vs. payment calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCH and MDH hospital‑specific rate selection rules
rubrics_metrics.description: SCHs are paid based on whichever yields greatest aggregate payment: the Federal national rate or updated hospital-specific rates based on FY1982, FY1987, FY1996, or FY2006 costs per discharge. MDHs (for discharges before Jan 1, 2027) are paid the higher of the Federal rate or Federal rate plus 75% of the difference between the Federal and hospital‑specific rate (based on FY1982, FY1987, or FY2002).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal citation: section 1886(b)(3)(C) of the Act and subsequent rules; MDH program extension affects FY2027 discharges prior to Jan 1, 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating hospital‑specific rates and budget neutrality adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicable percentage increases to hospital-specific rates for SCHs/MDHs equal the update factor set in section 1886(b)(3)(B)(i) and are subject to Affordable Care Act amendments; hospital‑specific rates are adjusted by MS‑DRG reclassification and recalibration budget neutrality factors and the permanent 10% cap on reduction in an MS‑DRG's relative weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See section V.F of the preamble and prior rules; the MS‑DRG 10% cap budget neutrality factor is applied where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital Federal rate update framework components (CIPI and adjustments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §412.308(c)(1) the capital standard Federal rate is updated using a capital input price index (CIPI) adjusted for case-mix changes, intensity, DRG reclassification/recalibration, and forecast error corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY2027 proposed update factor = 3.1% composed of projected CIPI increase (2.8%), 0.0 pp adjustments for intensity/case-mix/reclassification, and a 0.3 pp forecast error correction. CMS continues to use CIPI as the principal index for capital costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case‑mix index adjustment definition and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Case‑mix index measures average DRG weight; changes may reflect real patient resource use, documentation/coding changes, or reclassification/recalibration. The net case‑mix adjustment equals projected real case‑mix change minus projected total case‑mix change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY2027 CMS projects 0.5% real case-mix increase and proposes a 0.0 percentage point net adjustment (i.e., no net upward adjustment).

rubrics_metrics.name: DRG reclassification and recalibration adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustment to remove effects of prior years' DRG classification and weight changes to retain budget neutrality for case‑mix index related changes not due to patient severity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a two‑year data lag for evaluating reclassification effects; CMS proposes a 0.0 percentage point adjustment for FY2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forecast error adjustment threshold and application
rubrics_metrics.description: An adjustment for forecast error to the CIPI is made only if the absolute difference between actual and projected CIPI exceeds 0.25 percentage points; the forecast error is actual CIPI increase less the forecasted increase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS calculated a 0.3 percentage point forecast error for FY2025 (actual 2.9% vs forecast 2.6%), exceeding the 0.25 pp threshold, and thus proposes a forecast error correction in the FY2027 update.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensity adjustment methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Intensity adjustment reflects changes in utilization within DRG severity and adoption of quality‑enhancing services; CMS uses a Medicare-specific intensity measure based on a 5‑year average of cost per discharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method assumes one‑half of annual intensity change due to ineffective practice patterns and one‑half due to quality‑enhancing technologies; when intensity is declining CMS treats the adjustment as zero rather than negative. For FY2027 CMS proposes a 0.0 pp intensity adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capital outlier payment adjustment factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Under §412.308(c)(2) the capital Federal rate is reduced by an adjustment factor equal to the estimated proportion of capital-related outlier payments to total inpatient capital-related PPS payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS continues to incorporate estimated operating outlier reconciliation amounts into the outlier threshold model and will apply the analogous proportion for capital payments when estimating the capital Federal rate adjustment.
